subject: Hosted API onramp: access playbook & next steps
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Aurelia Chen <aurelia@blueharbor.ai>, Marc Ruiz <marc.ruiz@finlytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API onramp: access playbook & next steps

Hi Aurelia / Marc —

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great discussion on the ingestion pipeline and where model answers will be surfaced in FinLytics. Per our call, I wanted to pull together a short onramp playbook so your engineering team can validate hosted as a viable first step before we talk Dedicated or Private deployments.

Top items we need from you to scope the Hosted evaluation: 
- Expected steady-state QPS and peak bursts (requests/sec; include average tokens per request).
- Typical prompt length and max response length (tokens) for primary flows.
- Any PII/data residency constraints that would force Private/VPC instead of Hosted.
- Required SLA for 95th/99th latency (ms) and acceptable tail latencies.
- Whether you need IP allowlist or OAuth-based service accounts for keys.

Quickstart plan (what Redwood will provide):
1) Short-lived eval keys + a sandbox endpoint (managed, hosted).
2) Dedicated staging endpoints for your test traffic profile (rate-limited to your expected peak *2).
3) A one-pager ratecap & error pattern doc (attached: quickstart-checklist.pdf).
4) Two-week monitoring window with token-level cost estimates and latency histograms.

Decision signals that typically push customers from Hosted -> Dedicated:
- Sustained high RPS where unit cost on Hosted exceeds committed pricing threshold.
- Need for GPU isolation or strict throughput guarantees.
- Regulatory constraints requiring a customer-managed network.

Please reply with the bullet items above this week and I’ll provision the sandbox endpoints by Friday. I’ve attached the quickstart checklist and the SLA summary for reference.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
Attachment: quickstart-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)
Attachment: service-sla-summary.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Aurelia Chen <aurelia@blueharbor.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Cc: Steph Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Marc Ruiz <marc.ruiz@finlytics.com>
Date: 2026-08-27T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API onramp: access playbook & next steps

Neha —

Thanks for the clear summary. Quick answers from our side so you can size the sandbox: 
- Steady-state QPS: ~8 req/s during trading hours; peak bursts up to ~120 req/s for short windows (30–90s). Average tokens/request: 380 (prompt+response).
- Prompt patterns: mix of short (<64 tokens) and long analytic prompts (500–800 tokens) depending on batch enrichment jobs. Max response we expect ~1,200 tokens in a few reports.
- Data residency: EU market data must stay in-region; US analytics fine on US-hosted. For initial eval we'll send obfuscated samples, but eventual production will need EU residency for that dataset.
- SLAs: 95th < 250ms preferred for short prompts; long analytic jobs fine with higher latency but need throughput guarantees.
- Auth: prefer OAuth-based service accounts and IP allowlist for the sandbox.

We’re happy to try Hosted first for US workloads while we validate EU residency constraints. Can you confirm sandbox endpoints will allow region-specific routing? Also want to know the per-token rate-limiting behavior during bursts — is throttling token-based or request-based?

Thanks — I’ll loop in Marc if we need procurement info.

—Aurelia
Head of ML Platform, BlueHarbor (FinLytics pilot)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Aurelia Chen <aurelia@blueharbor.ai>, Marc Ruiz <marc.ruiz@finlytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Steph Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-27T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API onramp: access playbook & next steps

Aurelia —

Perfect, this is exactly the level of detail we need. Short answers inline and then next steps: 

- Region routing: yes — sandbox will include a US endpoint and an EU endpoint so you can validate residency behavior. We’ll tag requests by region and show token-level traces in the Console.
- Rate-limiting model: primarily request-based with token-aware soft-limits. For short prompts we throttle by requests/sec; for long analytic responses we also apply a token/sec window to avoid model starvation. In practice: bursts at 120 req/s for short prompts will be rate-limited at the endpoint (we can set a burst buffer). We’ll provide a suggested ratecap profile tuned to your traffic (attach sample).

Next steps I’ll take this afternoon: 
1) Provision two sandbox endpoints (us-east and eu-west) and generate OAuth service accounts + test keys.
2) Preconfigure a ratecap policy: steady 10 req/s (per key) with 300 req/s burst window across keys for short prompts, and a token/sec cap for long responses. We’ll tune after your test run.
3) Share a short-run test script (curl + python) to replay a representative traffic mix.
4) Schedule a 30-min check-in next Wed to walk through Console metrics and cost curves.

Action for you: confirm preferred window to run the burst test (we recommend a 30-minute window outside business opening at your end to avoid noise).

I’ll also flag this for Aditya and Steph to review if we see sustained peaks that would make Dedicated more cost-effective.

Thanks,
Neha
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
From: Marc Ruiz <marc.ruiz@finlytics.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Aurelia Chen <aurelia@blueharbor.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Steph Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-27T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API onramp: access playbook & next steps

Neha / team —

Thanks — we can run the burst test Friday 08/29 02:00–02:30 PT (outside our morning ingest). Aurelia will coordinate the obfuscated sample payloads. Two small procurement notes before we spin up keys: 
- Can Redwood provide a short PO template or MSA redline window if we decide to move beyond the eval? We’ll need that for internal approvals.
- Any uplift for EU-region hosted data residency or is that included in the Hosted plan?

Happy to proceed with the sandbox steps once those are clarified.

—Marc
Engineering Manager, FinLytics
